messages:
maya: Heads up — after the fp8 quant push the console heatmap anchoring for the token_loss chart is flipped in the diff view. baseline vs candidate look reversed, so alerts are noisy. cc @sam @alejandra :eyes:

sam: I noticed a CI alert for metric drift too. looks like the runner exported a different anchor key than the UI expects — maybe schema drift. Can you paste a repro?

ci-bot: eval-runner/quant-fp8 #1234 failed at 03:12 UTC
Logs:
```
ERROR: MetricAggregationError: aggregator 'anchor_mean' failed for metric 'token_loss'
Trace: KeyError('meta.anchor')
```

alejandra: Good catch. We moved to schema v3 last week; anchor moved from meta.anchor -> tags.anchor in the export mapping. UI still reads meta.anchor.

jon: Can you paste the runner command / config that reproduces this, maya?

maya: Repro steps (minimal):
```
# run locally
runner eval --model prod/v1-fp8 --dataset small_cohort --config-file ./ci/quant_test.yaml
# ci/quant_test.yaml (excerpt)
metrics:
  - name: token_loss
    aggregator: anchor_mean
    anchor_path: meta.anchor
runner:
  seed: null
  batch_size: 8
```
When seed is null the CI run sometimes flips the aggregate ordering. Setting seed=42 stabilizes it.

sam: aha — two issues then: (1) anchor path moved in the exported payload, (2) nondeterminism from batches/seed. The UI is probably reading a missing field and falling back to the wrong axis.

kevin: Quick mitigation: I can add a tolerant lookup in the backend that tries ['meta.anchor','tags.anchor','meta_tags.anchor'] before failing. Will open a hotfix PR. Also suggest a CI test asserting anchor presence.

alejandra: Longer term we should standardize the exporter flattening logic. The v3 exporter introduced dotpath flattening that renamed keys. I'll add a migration shim in the exporter. Also:+1 on an integration test for the diff view.

jon: For the runner nondeterminism — set runner.seed=42 in CI job config for the quant jobs. Also enforce batch_size=1 for the unit-level stability test; we can keep prod batch sizes but test with 1.

maya: Test snippet that reproduces flip locally:
```
# flip repro (runs produce different ordering w/o seed)
for i in 1 2 3; do runner eval --model prod/v1-fp8 --dataset small_cohort --config-file ./ci/quant_test.yaml; done
# with seed:
runner eval --model prod/v1-fp8 --dataset small_cohort --config-file ./ci/quant_test.yaml --override runner.seed=42
```

sam: I'll add a small runner unit test (test_heatmap_anchor) that writes two tiny runs and asserts identical ordering for anchor buckets.

kevin: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-platform/pull/987 (hotfix/backfill-anchor-shim) — adds tolerant lookup + small dashboard fallback. ci-bot, please re-run failing job. :shipit:

ci-bot: Re-run requested by kevin: eval-runner/quant-fp8 #1234 -> queued

maya: After kevin's local patch + setting seed=42 in the CI job the staging run matches baseline ordering. I'll follow up with a short runbook entry: "If diff heatmap appears reversed, check anchor_path + runner seed."

alejandra: I'll push exporter migration and an integration test that verifies anchoring across schema versions.

jon: Assignments: sam -> unit test in eval-harness, alejandra -> exporter shim + migration test, kevin -> hotfix PR & staging rollout, maya -> runbook + confirm prod flag.

kevin: Merged hotfix to staging branch, rolling to staging in 10m. will ping when sounds clear. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks all — recovering alert noise. Will keep thread updated if anything else pops up. :eyes:
